claims: The Artemis II mission is scheduled to splash down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego on Friday, April 10, 2026.
The Artemis II mission splashdown is scheduled at approximately 5:07 p.m. PDT.
The Artemis II mission splashdown is scheduled at 8:07 p.m. EDT.
The Artemis II mission splashdown location is off the coast of San Diego, California.
The crew of the Artemis II mission will be recovered by the USS John P. Murtha.
Live coverage of the Artemis II re-entry and landing will be available on NASA+.
Live coverage of the Artemis II re-entry and landing will be available on the NASA app.
Live coverage of the Artemis II re-entry and landing will be available on the NASA YouTube channel.
The service module separates from the crew module at approximately 6:33 p.m. CDT.
The service module separation is roughly 20 minutes before re-entry.
Coastal communities in San Diego County may hear or feel sonic booms between 5:00 and 5:15 p.m. PDT.
The USGS is monitoring the sonic booms.
The Artemis II mission has an 80% chance of favorable weather conditions for the reentry and recovery.
